questions.q: From where does God render judgment?
questions.a: God takes his place in the assembly that he governs and pronounces his judgments there.

questions.q: What does God say to the rulers in the assembly?
questions.a: God asks them how long they will judge unjustly and show favoritism to the wicked.

questions.q: What does God tell the rulers to do for the poor and the orphan?
questions.a: God tells them to judge the poor and the orphan fairly and to vindicate the poor and the destitute.

questions.q: What does God tell the rulers to do for the poor and needy?
questions.a: God tells them to rescue the poor and needy and deliver them from the hand of the wicked.

questions.q: What does God say about the rulers who do not know or understand?
questions.a: God says they walk about in darkness, foolishness, and ignorance, and no longer live by the basic principles that make a society fair.

questions.q: What does God say will happen to the gods he calls sons of the Most High?
questions.a: God says they will die like ordinary men and fall like one of the princes.

questions.q: Why does the psalmist ask God to arise and judge the earth?
questions.a: He asks God to judge the earth because God is the ruler of the nations.

commentary.text: Verses 1–5 Magistrates are the mighty in authority for the public good. Magistrates are the ministers of God's providence, for keeping up order and peace, and particularly in punishing evil-doers, and protecting those that do well. Good princes and good judges, who mean well, are under Divine direction; and bad ones, who mean ill, are under Divine restraint. The authority of God is to be submitted to, in those governors whom his providence places over us. But when justice is turned from what is right, no good can be expected. The evil actions of public persons are public mischiefs.

It is hard for men to have honour put upon them, and not to be proud of it. But all the rulers of the earth shall die, and all their honour shall be laid in the dust. God governs the world. There is a righteous God to whom we may go, and on whom we may depend. This also has respect to the kingdom of the Messiah. Considering the state of affairs in the world, we have need to pray that the Lord Jesus would speedily rule over all nations, in truth, righteousness, and peace.
